query: What review signals predict negative Amazon product satisfaction?

per_column.name: disappointment_signal
per_column.rationale: Presence of disappointment is a sentiment cue derived from review text that plausibly predicts satisfaction polarity without being a restatement of the label itself; it is an inferable feature, not the outcome. Mild leakage risk since it is emotionally near the label, but it remains a distinct extracted signal usable before knowing label_pos.

per_column.name: frustration_or_annoyance_tone
per_column.rationale: Tone categorization (frustration, annoyance, sarcasm) is a text-derived affective feature that carries genuine predictive signal about negative satisfaction while remaining distinct from the binary label; it captures gradations not deterministically equal to label_pos.

per_column.name: waste_or_resource_loss_framing
per_column.rationale: Whether the review frames the purchase as wasted money/time/effort is a specific rhetorical feature outside the label, plausibly correlated with dissatisfaction but not a restatement of it.

per_column.name: personal_inconvenience_or_burden
per_column.rationale: Categorizes concrete burdens (repeated effort, incompatibility, logistical, safety) that are content-grounded predictors of dissatisfaction; these are substantive drivers rather than restatements of the outcome and add non-trivial signal.

per_column.name: explicit_product_comparison
per_column.rationale: Type of comparison (to expectations, competitor, prior model) is a legitimate text-derived feature that lies outside the label and can carry predictive signal in either direction, making it a valid non-leaking predictor.

judge.rationale: All five columns are content-grounded, text-derived features that lie outside label_pos and none deterministically restate or are computable only after the outcome, so none are strict leakage. Several (disappointment_signal, frustration_tone) are affectively very close to the label, giving strong but partly redundant sentiment signal; the more diagnostic contributions come from concrete framings (waste, inconvenience/burden, comparison type) that decompose *why* a review is negative and add genuine leverage beyond raw title/content. As a set they provide moderate-to-good predictive leverage, tempered by overlap among the sentiment-oriented columns.
